problem
Three teams, three A.I. providers, three sets of keys, and three bills.
The invoice arrives, and nobody can say who spent what.
And when one provider goes down, so does your app.
fix
01  The fix
Fix found: Lite L.L.M., one gateway for more than a hundred A.I. providers.
Think of it as a switchboard for your A.I. calls.
The core is M.I.T. licensed, with over sixty thousand GitHub stars.
how
02  How it works
Your apps call one endpoint in the Open A.I. format, or use it as a Python library.
It checks the key, sends the call to the right provider, and logs what it cost.
uses
03  Three real uses
One. Switch models without rewriting code: the same call reaches Open A.I., Anthropic or Gemini. You change one name.
Two. Give each team its own key, with its own models, budget and rate limit. Once a key passes its budget, its requests fail.
Three. Stay up when a provider fails. It retries, spreads traffic across deployments, and falls back to another model.
catch
04  The catch
Now, the catch.
It's open core: single sign-on past five users, audit logs and secret managers need a paid licence.
Keys, budgets and spend tracking need a Postgres database, and more than one copy needs Redis too.
And it moves fast: a new minor version every week, so pin your version.
fit
05  Who it's for
It's for platform teams sharing many models across many apps, and Python developers who want one way to call them.
With one app and one provider, a gateway is probably more than you need.
Want an alternative? Take a look at Portkey Gateway.
try
06  Try it
To try it, follow the Docker quick start in their docs: it starts the gateway and a Postgres database. Then sign in to the admin page.
